presentingComplaint: Severe headache, blurred vision, and breathlessness for 6 hours
history: 58-year-old man with a 10-year history of poorly controlled hypertension (self-reported non-adherence to amlodipine and losartan for the past 2 months) presents with acute-onset severe occipital headache, blurred vision, and progressive breathlessness over the last 6 hours. He also reports two episodes of vomiting and mild chest tightness on exertion earlier today. No history of illicit drug use, no recent trauma, no fever. He has known type 2 diabetes mellitus. Family reports he appeared confused and slower to respond over the last hour.
examination: Anxious, breathless man sitting upright. Bilateral basal crackles on chest auscultation with raised JVP and mild bilateral ankle edema. Fundoscopy shows bilateral flame hemorrhages, cotton-wool spots, and early papilledema. Neurological exam shows mild disorientation to time (GCS 14/15) without focal deficit. No carotid or renal bruits. Cardiac exam reveals a loud S2 and S4 gallop without murmur.
imaging: Chest X-ray: bilateral perihilar haziness with pulmonary vascular congestion consistent with acute pulmonary edema
ECG: left ventricular hypertrophy with strain pattern, no acute ST-elevation
CT head (non-contrast): no acute hemorrhage or infarct; findings compatible with posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) pattern on subsequent MRI if performed
differentialDiagnoses: Hypertensive emergency with acute pulmonary edema and hypertensive encephalopathy
Acute coronary syndrome with secondary severe hypertension
finalDiagnosis: Hypertensive emergency (severe blood pressure elevation with acute target-organ damage: hypertensive encephalopathy, acute pulmonary edema/heart failure, and acute kidney injury)
contraindications: Avoid rapid/precipitous BP lowering (>25% within first hour) — risk of watershed cerebral/coronary/renal ischemia
Avoid nifedipine (immediate-release) sublingual for BP control
Avoid beta-blockade as first-line if acute decompensated pulmonary edema dominates without concurrent aortic dissection or ACS indication
Avoid clonidine or other agents causing rebound hypertension in a patient who may have erratic follow-up/adherence
edgeCases: If chest/back pain were tearing in quality or pulse/BP differential present, must exclude aortic dissection urgently (CT angiogram) before treating as isolated hypertensive emergency
Renal impairment may represent chronic kidney disease with acute-on-chronic injury versus purely acute hypertensive nephrosclerosis — need baseline creatinine
Pregnancy-associated severe hypertension (pre-eclampsia/eclampsia) is a distinct entity not applicable here (male patient)
Cocaine/sympathomimetic-induced hypertensive crisis excluded by history; if present would change drug choice (avoid unopposed beta-blockade)
expectedMaiK: MaiK should flag this as a hypertensive emergency with multi-organ involvement (encephalopathy, pulmonary edema, AKI) requiring immediate IV antihypertensive titration with a controlled, gradual BP reduction target (~25% MAP reduction in the first hour), continuous monitoring, and urgent exclusion of aortic dissection/ACS/stroke as mimics.
expectedNextQuestions: Is there tearing/radiating chest or back pain to suggest aortic dissection?
What is the patient's baseline/premorbid creatinine and blood pressure?
Any history of illicit sympathomimetic drug use (cocaine, amphetamines)?
Is the patient pregnant or postpartum (not applicable here but part of standard screen)?
Any visual field deficits or seizure activity suggesting evolving PRES?
